questions.q: What is the Analytics pane, in relation to a chart you've already built?
options: A completely separate visual you drag onto the canvas
A replacement for the Filters pane
A set of features layered on top of a supported visual — reference lines, error bars, forecasting, anomaly detection — not a separate visual type
A tool only available in the Power BI service, never Desktop
questions.explain: The Analytics pane adds capability to a visual you select — it doesn't create a new visual on its own.

questions.q: Besides an average line, what other reference line types does Power BI support?
options: Only lines based on the current date
Only average and median — no other options exist
Reference lines can only be added to tables, not charts
Min, max, median, percentile, and constant lines fixed to an axis value
questions.explain: You can add multiple line types, and even multiple instances of the same type (like a 25th and 75th percentile line together), each with its own name and formatting.

questions.q: What does the shaded band around a forecast represent?
options: The confidence interval — how certain the forecast is, widening the further out it predicts
An error in the underlying data model
The historical data range only
The forecast's sensitivity setting
questions.explain: The confidence interval reflects growing uncertainty the further into the future a forecast projects — it's part of what makes the prediction honest about its limits.

questions.q: Which visual types support forecasting and anomaly detection?
options: Tables and matrices only
All chart types support both features equally
Any visual with a numeric axis
Line charts only
questions.explain: Both forecasting and anomaly detection are restricted to line charts, since they depend on genuine time-series data along a continuous axis.

questions.q: What does the 'Explain by' setting do in anomaly detection?
options: Lets you point at other fields that might account for a flagged anomaly, surfacing a possible explanation when selected
Converts the anomaly into a new calculated column
Sets the forecast length
Automatically removes anomalies from the chart
questions.explain: When a viewer selects a flagged anomaly, Power BI can analyze the fields named in Explain by to suggest what might have caused the unexpected spike or dip.
